thumbnails.prompt_en: Photorealistic high-saturation HDR wide shot of a single naval pier in the Philippines in bright late-afternoon sun, just before golden hour. Moored side by side in one continuous scene: on the left, a small weathered gray 1980s Pohang-class corvette with rust streaks and scratched, pitted hull plates, touched by warm glowing orange sunlight; on the right, a much larger brand-new gray guided-missile frigate, its hull towering over the old ship, with crisp bright electric blue reflections from the sea and sky on its steel. A few Filipino sailors in blue working uniforms walk on the pier between them, small in the frame. Clear tropical water reflects both ships under a bright sky. Natural documentary realism, no oversized flags, no exaggerated faces, the size difference alone tells the story. On the pier in the foreground, a row of Korean navy sailors in white uniforms stand at attention with their backs half-turned to the camera, the bright electric blue harbor water behind them, watching the ship they once served on change hands. thumbnails.prompt_en: Photorealistic high-saturation HDR cinematic three-part composition in bright daylight. On the left, a weathered gray 1980s Korean-built Pohang-class corvette with rust streaks and scratched, battered steel sits in warm glowing orange haze, a single US 100-dollar bill floating large in the air before it, with a small plain Philippine flag on the upper left corner. In the center, an attractive Filipino naval officer with a warm likeable face in a white dress uniform, chest-up close-up filling 60 percent of the frame height, jaw-dropped and awestruck, looking toward the right. On the right, two brand-new gray guided-missile frigates sail forward in a heroic low-angle shot, lit by bright electric blue light with a thin golden rim light and lens flare, larger and closer than the old ship, and a huge Korean flag Taegukgi waves proudly in the upper right corner. Triumphant, victorious, epic mood.
